title: Serving a static file
summary: Nginx is a web server. It can answer a request by sending a file, such as index.html, without running a custom application backend.
introduction: Nginx is a web server. It can answer a request by sending a file, such as index.html, without running a custom application backend. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Nginx is a web server. It can answer a request by sending a file, such as index.html, without running a custom application backend.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These are configuration fragments unless shown as a whole structure. Do not change a system server. A separate local Nginx installation is optional; the tutorial application itself stays static.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Nginx. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Request: GET /index.html
Nginx reads: the configured index.html file
Response: HTML for the browser
blocks.title: Serving a static file

blocks.text: The browser then reads the HTML and may ask for CSS or images too.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw the requests needed for a page with one stylesheet.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Serving files is different from executing browser JavaScript on the server.
For more detail later, use this [Nginx further reading](https://nginx.org/en/docs/beginners_guide.html).

seo.title: Nginx: Serving a static file
